timeline.event: The Olmec city of San Lorenzo flourishes on the Gulf coast
timeline.label: c. 1200 BCE

timeline.event: The Pyramid of the Sun rises at Teotihuacan
timeline.label: c. 200 CE

timeline.event: Pakal the Great becomes ruler of the Maya city of Palenque
The Mexica found Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco
timeline.label: c. 1325

timeline.event: Hernán Cortés's expedition reaches the Mexican coast
Tenochtitlan falls to Spanish and allied Indigenous forces
The Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico is founded
Miguel Hidalgo issues the Cry of Dolores
Mexico wins independence from Spain
Texas declares independence from Mexico
The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends the Mexican-American War
Mexican forces defeat the French at the Battle of Puebla
Emperor Maximilian is executed and the Republic restored
The Mexican Revolution begins
A new Constitution is proclaimed in Querétaro
President Lázaro Cárdenas nationalizes the oil industry
Mexico City hosts the Summer Olympic Games
A powerful earthquake devastates Mexico City
The North American Free Trade Agreement takes effect
Vicente Fox's election ends seven decades of PRI presidencies

places.name: Mexico City
places.clue: Built on the drained lakebed of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, parts of the city are still sinking every year.

places.name: Chichén Itzá
places.clue: At the equinoxes, shadows on El Castillo's staircase form the illusion of a serpent slithering down the pyramid.

places.name: Cancún
places.clue: Its hotel zone sits on a narrow 7-shaped sandbar between the Caribbean Sea and the Nichupté Lagoon.

places.name: Guadalajara
places.clue: Mariachi music and tequila both trace their roots to the countryside around this western city.

places.name: Cabo San Lucas
places.clue: Its famous rock arch, El Arco, stands at the tip of Baja California where the Pacific meets the Gulf of California.

places.name: Copper Canyon
places.clue: This network of gorges in the Sierra Madre Occidental is larger, and in places deeper, than the Grand Canyon.

places.name: Monte Albán
places.clue: The Zapotecs flattened a mountaintop to build this ceremonial city high above the Oaxaca Valley.

places.name: Palenque
places.clue: Its jungle temples hid the tomb of King Pakal, discovered in 1952 deep beneath the Temple of the Inscriptions.

places.name: Popocatépetl
places.clue: One of the country's most active volcanoes, its Nahuatl name means 'Smoking Mountain'.

places.name: Guanajuato
places.clue: Its colourful colonial streets run partly through tunnels, and its silver mines were once among the richest in the world.

places.name: Cuatro Ciénegas
places.clue: Desert pools here shelter living stromatolites, giving scientists a glimpse of what early life on Earth looked like.

places.name: El Pinacate
places.clue: Its giant volcanic craters looked lunar enough that Apollo astronauts trained among them before going to the Moon.
